title: Beehiiv Expands Roster of Creators With Dana Harris-Bridson, David Covucci and Peter Greenberg
description: Beehiiv, the creator platform that has gained traction through associations with independent journalists such as Oliver Darcy and Joanna Stern, unve
body:
Beehiiv, the creator platform that has gained traction through associations with independent journalists such as Oliver Darcy and Joanna Stern, unveiled an expansion of its Media Collective, a roster of journalists who have turned to the company to help launch new digital efforts.

	The new creators are Peter Greenberg, a longtime travel editor at CBS News; Dana Harris-Birdson, former editor in chief of IndieWire; and tech and politics reporter David Covucci.
	

	Beehiiv launched the Media Collective in 2024, offering support in areas such as legal, healthcare, technology, audience, monetization and other operations, while journalists tend to their work and business.


	“We started the Media Collective to solve a problem I kept hearing from journalists: they wanted to bet on themselves, but going independent meant losing the support system they had spent their careers relying on,” said Tyler Denk, co-founder and CEO of Beehiiv, in a statement. “The Media Collective gives them the scaffolding to build something of their own while staying focused on what they do best: reporting. It’s grown faster and been more successful than we anticipated.”

	The company said its “collective” now includes more than 30 journalists, who together reach more than 1 million active subscribers. Media Collective members keep 100% of the revenue they earn.

	 Greenberg will on September 15 launch “The Upgrade,” reporting on things of key interest to travelers, including airline and hotel practices, cruise ship safety, loyalty programs, travel disruptions and the oversight of aircraft maintenance and airworthiness. Greenberg hosts and produces three long-running television programs: “The Royal Tour,” “Hidden,” and “The Travel Detective.” 
	

	Harris-Bridson will launch Flamingo Media in January, 2027. Flamingo will cover what Harris-Bridson calls the “Story Economy,” the increasingly interconnected market spanning entertainment, creators, brands, platforms, technology and capital.

	 Covucci, a former editor with The Daily Dot and Uproxx Media, recently started FOIAball, an independent investigative publication that uses public-records laws to uncover stories tied to college sports, including political influence, surveillance technology, labor rights and wealthy donors.

schema.headline: Beehiiv Expands Roster of Creators With Dana Harris-Bridson, David Covucci and Peter Greenberg

title: Ginevra Elkann’s ‘The Roses of Marrakesh,’ Starring Fanny Ardant, Boarded by True Colours (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Rome-based sales company True Colours has boarded Italian director Ginevra Elkann’s new feature “The Roses of Marrakesh” (“Le Rose di Marrakech”) st
body:
Rome-based sales company True Colours has boarded Italian director Ginevra Elkann’s new feature “The Roses of Marrakesh” (“Le Rose di Marrakech”) starring Fanny Aradant as an aged matron named Madame Isabelle who lives in a luxurious estate in the Palmeraie of Marrakech.

	Elkann, who is a granddaughter of former Fiat automaker chief Gianni Agnelli, is a London Film School graduate who worked as an assistant to Bernardo Bertolucci and Anthony Minghella. She made her directorial debut with “Magari” (“If Only”), a semi-autobiographical comedy about the disconnect felt by kids with divorced parents that opened the Locarno Film Festival in 2019. She followed with the black comedy “I Told You So” that launched from Toronto in 2023. “The Roses of Marrakesh,” her third feature,  is set in the famous Agnelli estate in Marrakech known as Aïn Kassimou.
	

	The story follows Leila, the devoted housekeeper at the estate of Madame Isabelle, who “maintains the careful order of this timeless bubble, where everyone plays their role to perfection,” says the provided synopsis. “Between her and Yusef, the head gardener, a tacit, quiet, and restrained friendship has formed. When Leila’s sister arrives unexpectedly, revealing a heavy secret from their past, the tranquillity of this microcosm begins to crack,” it adds.


	Nisrin Erradi, Ahmed Hammoud, Jalila Talemsi and Boubker Fahmi star alongside Ardant. 

	Lucky Red will handle distribution in Italy of “The Roses of Marrakesh,” which is completed.

	True Colours will be launching international sales of the film in Toronto.
	

	“The Roses of Marrakesh is a small story, and I mean that as praise,” Ginevra Elkann said in a statement.

	 “It’s about love, about the ordinary business of surviving our own pain, and about the tenderness we find along the way,” she added. “I made it close to the bone, because that’s the only place where I know how to find something true — and therefore universal.”

	Commented True Colours MD Elliot Gustin-Hollman: “‘The Roses of Marrakesh’ is a beautiful film about the friendship between two women that transcends their fate.” 

	“We believe it’s exactly the kind of poetic movie audiences are looking for right now, and we’re truly proud to be working with a talented director like Ginevra.”

schema.headline: Ginevra Elkann’s ‘The Roses of Marrakesh,’ Starring Fanny Ardant, Boarded by True Colours (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Jeff Goldblum on Being Honored by Oceana and Hosting ‘SNL U.K.’ Season 2 Premiere: ‘I’m a Big Anglophile’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
It’s just a couple of days before Jeff Goldblum is getting ready to head to London to host the Season 2 premiere of “SNL U.K.” on Sept. 12.

	“I’m a
body:
It’s just a couple of days before Jeff Goldblum is getting ready to head to London to host the Season 2 premiere of “SNL U.K.” on Sept. 12.

	“I’m a big Anglophile,” he tells me on a Zoom from Italy, where he and his wife Emilie are enjoying a summer vacation. “I’ve read all of P.G. Wodehouse. We recently filmed ‘Wicked’ there, and I did the last ‘Jurassic’ movie there. I’ve spent a lot of time in London. I’ve done a couple of things on the West End. I’m a big fan. I’m excited and humbled and thrilled to be part of it.”
	

	Goldblum is a two-time host of “Saturday Night Live” in the U.S. in 1993 and 1997.


	“It’ll get your blood going and put you on alert,” he recalls. “It’s a fun, exciting, creatively chaotic and delicious week. It seems they’re following something of the same schedule this week. I kind of remember it in my bones. When you finally get yourself out there, you’re trying to just do the assignment. It’s a blast.”

	Just three days after “SNL,” Goldblum and Emilie will be honored at Oceana’s annual New York gala at the Rainbow Room at Rockefeller Center on Sept. 15 for their work over the last almost 20 years championing the organization and its work to protect the world’s oceans. Martha Stewart will be named this year’s Ocean Champion. Sam Waterston, an Ocean Board member, will serve as master of ceremonies. The evening will mark Oceana’s 25th anniversary.

	Goldblum was first introduced to Oceana through his manager Keith Attis, who is a longtime environmental activist. The Goldblums’ love of the water even inspired their sons’ names, Charlie Ocean, 11 and River Joe, 9.
	

	“Charlie Ocean is so named apropos because he cannot stay out of that water, like just in and out, in and out, swimming all day long, body surfing,” Emilie says.



	

					Emilie and Jeff Goldblum attend Oceana: Sting Under the Stars on July 18, 2016, in Los Angeles.
									Penske Media via Getty Images
	



	The couple also loved the ocean when they were kids. Jeff and his family would travel from their Pittsburgh-area home to Atlantic City in the summer. “I have a memory of my mother taking me into the ocean and holding me in her arms, cradling me in her arms and feeling for the first time waves,” he says. “I didn’t know about waves. Like what’s this movement in the water going up and down and up and down, bobbing up and down?”

	Emilie, who grew up in Canada, spent time at the beach when she visited her grandparents in France. “There would be these little campgrounds, and we’d always camp close to an ocean,” she says. “That’s where we’d spend the whole day, and I would do gymnastics on the beach, tumbling and playing.”

	Jeff joined Oceana in lobbying California lawmakers in Sacramento in support of SB 54, regulations that aim to decrease single-use packaging and plastic waste. The act was signed into law by Gov. Gavin Newsom in 2022. To date, Oceana has contributed $20 million to support policy victories throughout the world.

	 “It’s magical,” Jeff says of the world’s oceans. “It’s part of our paradise of a planet. And woe be us, and shame on us if we don’t do everything to counteract the damage we’ve already begun.”

schema.headline: Jeff Goldblum on Being Honored by Oceana and Hosting ‘SNL U.K.’ Season 2 Premiere: ‘I’m a Big Anglophile’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Halloween Film Festival Launched by Ripcord; Indie Platform Aims to Connect Filmmakers With Genre Fans (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Ripcord, a new independent film platform that aims to directly connect genre filmmakers with fans, has announced a spooky new film festival.

	The H
body:
Ripcord, a new independent film platform that aims to directly connect genre filmmakers with fans, has announced a spooky new film festival.

	The Halloween Film Festival is set to showcase 50 short genre films, including horror, sci-fi, thriller and fantasy titles and fans can vote on their favorites. The winning entry will win $100,000 and the remaining nine films will split a $100,000 total prize, based on ranking, following a live screening at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Los Angeles on Oct. 29.
	

	The festival runs from Oct. 19-29, and all screenings are free to watch at ripcord.film. Filmmakers can submit their shorts via FilmFreeway (https://filmfreeway.com/RipcordHalloweenFilmFestival).


	The festival is the launch event for Ripcord, which is described per the company’s official release as “built to close one of independent cinema’s biggest gaps: exceptional films that struggle to find distribution and audiences who struggle to discover them. Rather than relying on traditional distributors, Ripcord lets filmmakers bring their work directly to fans. On Ripcord, fans can discover new creators, follow and interact with the filmmakers behind the films they love and purchase films directly to support them.”

	“Too many great independent films never find an audience, not because they aren’t good enough, but because the traditional path to distribution shuts most filmmakers out entirely,” Charlie Cleveland, the founder of Ripcord, said in a statement. “Ripcord exists to remove that gatekeeper and provide filmmakers with a direct line to the fans who are hungry for their work, and give those fans a real hand in discovering what’s next. This festival is the first step in building that home.”
	

	The festival is curated by program director Vanessa Meyer, who is the current head of The Genre Film Lab (GEMS) and was formerly programming director with the Frontières International Co-Production Market and programmer for Brooklyn Horror Film Festival and Reel Love Film Festival. John Hegeman, CCO of Wayward Entertainment and formerly the president of Orion Pictures and Blumhouse Tilt, Stacy Jorgensen, producer and former COO of SpectreVision, and Cleveland serve as festival directors.

schema.headline: Halloween Film Festival Launched by Ripcord; Indie Platform Aims to Connect Filmmakers With Genre Fans (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Disclosure Day’ Sets Peacock Streaming Release Date
description:
Steven Spielberg‘s latest sci-fi adventure, “Disclosure Day,” will stream on Peacock starting Oct. 9

	Emily Blunt and Josh O’Connor star as a meteo
body:
Steven Spielberg‘s latest sci-fi adventure, “Disclosure Day,” will stream on Peacock starting Oct. 9

	Emily Blunt and Josh O’Connor star as a meteorologist and whistleblower who discover an unexpected connection with alien life. They risk their lives to reveal the truth to the world about extraterrestrial activity and abuse at the hands of the U.S. government. The film, released in theaters on June 12, also stars Colman Domingo, Colin Firth, Wyatt Russell, Eve Hewson and newcomer Courtney Grace. 
	

	“Disclosure Day” grossed $241 million worldwide at the summer box office. Universal spent $115 million to produce it and $80 million to market the action drama. Overall, the film received positive reviews from critics, with an 80% on Rotten Tomatoes, while audiences were a bit more muted. In his review, Variety‘s chief film critic Owen Gleiberman commended the performances but concluded that the film “doesn’t take us anywhere overly surprising” by the end.


	Spielberg has won multiple Oscars over the course of his accomplished career, including best director and best picture for “Schindler’s List” and best director for “Saving Private Ryan,” along with many other nominations for films like “Raiders of the Lost Ark,” “Munich,” “War Horse,” “Lincoln,” “The Post” and “West Side Story.” He was most recently nominated for best picture as a producer on “Hamnet,” directed by Chloé Zhao.

	“Disclosure Day” continues Spielberg’s love for exploring the extraterrestrial, with some of his biggest hits including “E.T.” and “Close Encounters of the Third Kind.”

schema.headline: ‘Disclosure Day’ Sets Peacock Streaming Release Date

title: Sydney Sweeney Goes Nude in Provocative Ad for Novig Sports Trading App
description: Sydney Sweeney stripped down for a steamy new ad for Novig, the latest sports betting app and prediction marketing for fans of football, baseball, s
body:
Sydney Sweeney stripped down for a steamy new ad for Novig, the latest sports betting app and prediction marketing for fans of football, baseball, soccer, tennis and more. The “Euphoria” star goes nude in the ad and poses with a variety of sports equipment, like footballs, basketballs, a hockey net and other athletic gear. She also joins Novig as a strategic partner and equity holder.

	“The campaign was about embracing a fun idea,” said Sweeney in a statement. “The concept is simple: cut through the noise and put the focus entirely on sports. The campaign brings that idea to life with confidence, humor and a playful edge.”
	

	“Think you know sports? Prove it. Novig is just sports. So they wanted to show just sports,” Sweeney says as she poses nude atop a basketball hoop and covers herself with basketballs and footballs.


	The ad continues with a provocative montage of Sweeney in different athletic uniforms, like a hockey goalie’s mask, football pads, a baseball catcher’s helmet and a Novig jersey. After repeating the word “sports” several times, she breaks a set of racked billiard balls and lies on top of the pool table: “You can’t trade this. I just look good here,” she says.

	Novig launched nationwide last month under a federally regulated framework. The platform has a 21+ age requirement and combines the mechanics of modern financial exchanges with a sports-first experience.

	In the ad, Sweeney also clarifies that there’s “no betting on wars or deaths and no politics,” such as other popular prediction markets like Polymarket and others. “Just you, your takes and sports,” she says (while posing nude with a soccer ball).
	

	“Sports fans deserve a prediction market built specifically for them,” said Jacob Fortinsky, co-founder and CEO of Novig. “There are many places where people can engage with prediction markets across different categories. Our focus is sports, and by dedicating ourselves entirely to sports, we have built a better experience for fans. Sydney helped bring that message to life in a way that’s impossible to ignore.”

	The Novig ad is the latest steamy promotional that Sweeney has starred in; she’s posted several risqué videos for her lingerie brand Syrn that she launched early this year. She also starred in a jeans ad for American Eagle that many people found controversial online due to its play on “good genes.”

	In the film world, Sweeney will next star in “The Housemaid’s Secret,” the sequel to her hit adaptation of “The Housemaid” novel last year. Just like her rom-com “Anyone but You,” Sweeney turned the indie movie into a surprise box-office smash that grossed $400 million. Next up, she’s also got Netflix’s “Gundam” movie on her slate, along with StudioCanal’s “The Custom of the Country.”

	Watch the full Novig ad below.

title: ‘Bleeding Hearts’: This Must-See TIFF Doc Is a Real Life ‘A Star Is Born’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Love is a burning thing, a Man in Black once said, and its flame burns bright in “Bleeding Hearts,” an achingly intimate new documentary that captur
body:
Love is a burning thing, a Man in Black once said, and its flame burns bright in “Bleeding Hearts,” an achingly intimate new documentary that captures a country music couple falling for one another as their band embarks on its first cross-country tour.

	Directed by Andrew Morgan and making its world premiere at TIFF, the film chronicles a year in the life of Chaparelle, a country supergroup of sorts comprised of Zella Day, a former pop singer who’s opened for Lana Del Rey; country singer-songwriter Jesse Woods; and producer Beau Bedford. But it’s really more of a two-hander with Zella and Jesse, the couple at its center, harmonizing heartfelt ballads with one another.
	

	And they couldn’t be more different. Jesse, tall and taciturn, enjoys his alone time, favoring the solitary nature of the songwriting process over performing. He is prone to suffocating bouts of depression and was at a particularly low point when Stella entered his life. Stella is a tiny ball of energy who lights up every room she’s in and stage she sets foot on. She is also 12 years younger than her counterpart, who is 43.


	“Zella and I are very opposite in a lot of ways,” offers Woods. “I’m more of a stoic with a minimal amount of communication. Zella is a joyful person and it’s very good medicine for me.”

	“It’s like stars and gravity,” adds Day. “You have to be standing on the ground in order to look up and see the stars. For me, what Jesse brings to Chaparelle is this gravity.”

	If this juxtaposition — that of the tortured songwriter and eager ingénue who pulls him out of the darkness — sounds familiar, it is. You’ve seen it before in films like “Walk the Line” and, of course, three different versions of “A Star Is Born.” It’s hard not to think of “A Star Is Born” while watching “Bleeding Hearts,” as Woods and Day bask in quietude and tenderness at their Wimberley cabin before stepping under the bright lights to stomp, clap and croon, with Day firmly front and center.
	

	“I think they are two people who are in love with each other in a very honest way, and that honesty comes out when they perform,” explains Morgan. “Stella is a star. She has that extra something and she has it onstage, so it’s cool that she found someone in Jesse who’s not trying to outdo that and is allowing her to be that.”



	

					Day and Woods in “Bleeding Hearts.”
									TIFF
	



	Day and Woods seemed to find each other at just the right time. Woods had moved out to a cabin in Wimberley, a remote area in Texas with a population of 2,800 people. He’d “gone through a breakup, was drinking way too much and was isolated.” Day had been living in Los Angeles for thirteen years trying to break big as a pop star, which left her “spiritually and energetically” drained. She was tired of asking her more famous friends for favors and the transactional nature of L.A. She was “starved for authenticity” and needed to escape.

	“I was getting to a point where I was getting exhausted by the industry,” says Day. “I’d signed a record and publishing deal when I was 18 years old, and my whole life was built around my image and my music. I got to a point around 26 where I was exhausted by that, and my relationships were also exhausted by that. I hadn’t hit a stride where I’d reached a certain level of fame or success where it made things easier. I didn’t know how to move forward in a way that made my soul happy.”

	Day was a fan of Woods’ music, and in 2021, reached out to see if he’d like to write together. The two met at Austin City Limits, took in each other’s shows, and a month later he brought her out to Wimberley, which to her felt “so familiar and nostalgic,” like her cozy hometown of Pinetop, Arizona. The visits became more frequent, and before long, they were romantically and creatively conjoined. During one of those Wimberley trips, Bedford was invited out to the cabin, and the trio wrote the songs “Bleeding Hearts” and “Bad Loving” over the course of two days. Chaparelle was born.

	Shortly thereafter, a friend of Morgan’s sent him an unreleased demo of Chaparelle’s song “Bleeding Hearts,” a stirring, slow-burn duet with Day and Woods joining forces on the chorus: “A bleeding heart / Will make a mess of things / A falling star / Will burn up everything.” Morgan was immediately hooked.
	

	“I had a visceral reaction to that song in the same way I would as a kid if you heard a needle-drop song in a Cameron Crowe film that you hadn’t heard before,” he recalls. “Something lit up inside me.”



	The filmmaker reached out to the couple, who said they’d just started a relationship and a band. It had been a dream of Morgan’s to make a music film in real time, so he told Day and Woods he was interested in documenting “the first year of a band where it’s volatile and exciting and you don’t know what’s going to happen.” He asked them to be “all-in,” and, flattered by the director’s fandom, they agreed.

	“We didn’t sign a contractual obligation that we would never stop filming even if we weren’t OK with the process,” says Day. “It was this relationship we agreed to and every step of the way we decided we wanted to go further because we liked him and felt he was documenting a very special time in our lives.”

	“That’s what we do,” adds Woods. “We start new things and see how they go.”

	Morgan began shadowing them a few weeks later, in January of 2024, documenting their first shows on the West Coast. He would trail them for a year.

	“When I talked to them, I had been watching ‘Don’t Look Back’ and ‘Truth or Dare’ — films that were intimate in their nature — and that was really what I pitched them,” shares Morgan. “I wanted the audience to be in the hotels and in the vans with them.”

	Morgan, along with his longtime cinematographer, Lance Kuhns, tested a number of different looks for the film. There was something about Day and Woods’ story that struck them as timeless, so, like “Don’t Look Back” and “Truth or Dare,” they opted for black and white. And it’s a good thing they did because the film looks stunning.



	

					Andrew Morgan shooting “Bleeding Love.” 
									TIFF
	



	The team accomplished this with Sony FX6 and FX3 cameras, coupled with old prime lenses, and a group of five with Chaparelle on the road: Morgan; his brother/producer Zach; Kuhns; second DP Helen Cassell; and their sound mixer, Michael Flowe. Money, as you can imagine, was tight.  

	“I’m not supposed to say the exact number since we’re in sales talks, but I will say it’s less than you can physically imagine. The budget was really small,” Morgan attests. “We shot on small cameras, didn’t use lights and it was simple. We made it the way we used to make stuff in the backyard. We shot it like a home video the way you’d make something with your friends. There’s no one famous in this movie and no big company behind this movie. It was done piece by piece, and I’m incredibly proud of it.”
	

	“Bleeding Hearts” isn’t all sunshine and rainbows. We are treated to scenes of Day and Woods bickering over their contrasting approaches to live performance and conflict resolution in vans and backrooms, sometimes moments before they’re set to take the stage.

	“I think the hard part, for me, is I come from a genre of music where there’s not really banter or personality content on stage, and Zella comes from the pop world where a lot of it is speaking to the fans,” Woods says. “Where we clash, really, is Zella is like, ‘Talk to them more!’ And I’m like, ‘Talk to them less!’”

	“But then I’ll be like, ‘Let’s at least talk to each other.’ We still have this contrasting issue,” Day remarks. “He is so magnetic in a different way than I am and it’s something I want people to see. I want to be a projector of his light. It’s less wanting him to be something he’s not and more wanting him to share who he is, which in some ways is Jesse’s allure, that he doesn’t show very much.”

	We also see Day and Woods struggle with the realities of being a new touring band today that refuses to play by the new set of rules — namely, generating a barrage of social media content to promote your music and tour (or having someone generate it for you).

	“I really don’t love making content and Zella is younger and doesn’t particularly like doing it either. We want to get in the game and play the game, but there’s a line of, ‘I’m not going to do a dance or videos of me making breakfast,’” says Woods. “I still believe that if the music is good and you’re consistent, then good things will happen. Big Thief is one of my favorite bands and they’re an example of a band that did it the old way of playing amazing shows that created word of mouth. It’s still possible.”

	At one point, a major A&R representative even suggests Day re-record all of Chaparelle’s music without Woods if she wants to get signed, which gives them a good laugh. They may not be making money yet from Chaparelle, but the pair say they’re at least pulling in enough to keep the project going. And more importantly, they’ve never been happier.

	“We live humbly in the country with good food by a beautiful river, so we’ve got what we need covered,” Day maintains. “I know people who are incredibly successful and incredibly lonely, and I’m so grateful that that’s not me and my experience.”

schema.headline: ‘Bleeding Hearts’: This Must-See TIFF Doc Is a Real Life ‘A Star Is Born’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Box Office: ‘Practical Magic 2’ Aims to Dethrone ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ With $40 Million Debut
description:
After a summer for the record books, movie theater operators are hoping to keep the vibes high with some midnight margaritas.

	Those celebratory co
body:
After a summer for the record books, movie theater operators are hoping to keep the vibes high with some midnight margaritas.

	Those celebratory cocktails are part of the fun in “Practical Magic 2,” a fantasy sequel about witchy sisters played by Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock. Nostalgia should propel the follow-up film to $30 million to $40 million from 4,000 North American theaters in its debut, enough to claim No. 1 and topple the six-weekend reign of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.”
	

	“Practical Magic 2” is aiming for another $18 million to $25 million at the international box office from 77 territories, which would put initial global sales anywhere from $48 million to $65 million. Warner Bros. produced the movie for $75 million.


	The first “Practical Magic” was a box office flop but eventually became a cult favorite. In the original movie, based on the novel by Alice Hoffman, sisters Sally and Gillian Owens, who descend from a long line of witches, find themselves fighting off a curse that kills the men they fall in love with. Susanne Bier directed the sequel, which picks up 25 years later as Sally and Gillian’s daughters uncover their hidden family secrets and seek to break the curse that has long haunted their lineage. Dianne Wiest and Stockard Channing reprised their roles from the prior film, while Joey King and Maisie Williams joined the cast. Reviews for “Practical Magic 2” have not been kind (Variety’s critic Todd Gilchrist called the movie “as cumbersome and overlong as the 28-year wait” between the two chapters) — which may not bode well for box office longevity beyond its opening weekend.
	

	Also new to theaters is Disney’s music documentary “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger,” which is eyeing a $5 million to $7 million start from 1,200 domestic theaters. The concert film follows Liam and Noel Gallagher of the legendary British band Oasis as they reunite for the first time since 2009. Along with behind-the-scenes footage from their hugely successful world tour, “Don’t Look Back in Anger” boasts the first joint interview in two decades with the brothers, who famously don’t get along. Reception has been rapturous for the “Oasis” doc, which bowed earlier this week at Venice Film Festival.

	As the fall season slowly ramps up, summer leftovers like “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” “The Odyssey” and “Coyote vs. Acme” will round out box office charts. In the coming days, “Brand New Day” should supplant 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” ($936 million, not adjusted for inflation) as the highest-grossing movie of all time at the domestic box office. So far, Tom Holland’s latest adventure as Peter Parker has generated $923 million in North America and $2.4 billion globally.

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘Practical Magic 2’ Aims to Dethrone ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ With $40 Million Debut

title: Sony Pictures Entertainment CEO on Success of ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’: The Movie Is ‘Emotional’ and ‘Some People Come Away Crying’
description: The stunning box-office success of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” stems from the movie’s emotional impact — which is unlike other recent superhero movi
body:
The stunning box-office success of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” stems from the movie’s emotional impact — which is unlike other recent superhero movies, according to Sony Pictures Entertainment chairman and CEO Ravi Ahuja.

	Ahuja exulted in the blockbuster’s record-breaking run, which has smashed box office expectations by raking in more than $2.4 billion worldwide, ranking as the third-biggest theatrical release ever.


	“It’s a tremendous result. We obviously hadn’t forecast that. We thought it would do incredibly well, but we didn’t know that would do that well,” said Ahuja, speaking Wednesday at the BofA Securities 2026 Media, Communications & Entertainment Conference in New York.
	

	Ahuja said that with “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” “really everybody came together to create a great thing.” But, he added, “the movie itself is very emotional… So a little bit different to what some of the more recent superhero movies have been. Still very much a superhero movie — there are a lot of big action scenes. It’s a lot of fun. But it’s emotional. Some people come away crying, so that is something clearly that resonated with the audience.”

	“Brand New Day’s” high audience Rotten Tomato and CinemaScore ratings come down to “the incredible creative team.” That includes director Destin Daniel Cretton and the cast led by Tom Holland, Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, John Bernthal and Sadie Sink. “Our producers Kevin Feige, Amy Pascal did an amazing job, and our film studio also did a tremendous job in the marketing and the distribution,” Ahuja said, adding that it was distributed to more than 80,000 worldwide screens at the same time, which was a record.
	

	Ahuja said “Spider-Man” is one of SPE’s three biggest franchises, alongside “Jeopardy!” and “Wheel of Fortune.” About Spider Man, he said, “there’s so much appeal to the character of Peter Parker. So much appeal to the character, but you got to execute it right. And this movie really did.” When’s the next one coming out? Ahuja said, “We don’t have a date for it yet. A couple years usually, but there’s a Spider-Verse movie coming next year.”

	RELATED: Tom Rothman on Sony’s ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Blockbuster Success, Being Outbid for ‘Obsession’ and More

	Ahuja also spoke about the advantage Sony Pictures Entertainment has with its position as an “arms dealer” to the rest of the industry, because it’s an independent studio that doesn’t have a general-entertainment streaming arm. And he also said SPE isn’t interested in engaging with large-scale M&A at this point.

	The CEO addressed Sony Pictures Entertainment’s exclusive worldwide pay-one windowing output deal with Netflix, after theatrical and home entertainment, which was the first of its kind in the industry.

	“For one, it speaks to the value of the theatrical model. So by being dedicated to theatrical, it creates a very high bar for the movies that you can make. For example, we can’t make 30 or 40 movies. You can make about a dozen really big movies because they all have to meet that threshold, and there’s a lot of marketing that follows it,” Ahuja said.

	“So our movies do very well when they’re on Netflix or wherever they go. It also says as an independent studio, we’re able to do a deal like that. If we had our own streaming service, we wouldn’t do a global pay-one output deal. We’d keep the movies for ourselves. And the fact that there’s no other large studio that does that puts a lot of value on our output, so I think it speaks to the to the value of the strategy.” 

	The pay-one deal with Netflix “gives us is a lot more certainty and the ability to take some creative risk. As we know how globally it’s going to pay off when we achieve a particular result in box office.”

	Netflix also released Sony’s musical animated movie “K-Pop Demon Hunters,” which became a roaring success in 2025 “It seems very obvious now, but at the time it was first being developed in 2021, Netflix felt like the right home, and I’d argue it really was the right home,” Ahuja said. “I mean, if you look at the trajectory of ‘K-Pop Demon Hunters,’ it didn’t start that strong, but it built over time. So the Netflix platform really helped to build ‘K-Pop Demon Hunters.’ Had it been theatrical, I mean, boy, this is such a hypothetical. Who knows if it would have had a big opening weekend? But it’s done incredibly well on Netflix.” Ahuja added that SPE is working on a sequel for Netflix.
	

	Regarding “K-Pop Demon Hunters,” Ahuja said, “By being platform agnostic and content-focused, we’re able to build that franchise by hitting people in different places, when you really wouldn’t do that if you were just stuck in one platform. We’re able to benefit from media fragmentation and to really build these content assets and to build franchises.”

	Ahuja became CEO of Sony Pictures Entertainment in January 2025, after previously serving as SPE’s president and COO. He stepped down from the board of Roku (which recently struck a $22 billion deal to be acquired by Fox Corp.) shortly after he took the helm at Sony Pictures Entertainment.

	Asked about Sony Pictures Entertainment’s interest in mergers or acquisitions, Ahuja said “mega M&A, if you call it that, buying a diversified large-scale media company or merging with one, isn’t our priority for us.” That’s because “it’s very disruptive. Getting a deal done, getting a deal approved, the integration work — it sets you back for years. And this industry is dynamic and evolving, and you really have to position yourself for how it’s going to evolve over the next five to 10 years, not just drown in M&A. Particularly when I am doubtful of having increased scale and content creation making a big difference. These companies are not factories, right?”

	Ahuja recalled that SPE was interested in a deal to buy Paramount Global in 2024 together with private equity firm Apollo Global Management. “We were interested in it briefly, but [that was really more about the IP,” he said. “So it’s consistent with the strategy of looking for IP and capabilities.” But Ahuja said that, at that time, a deal to acquire Paramount would raised issues with CBS stations being owned by a non-U.S. company, and “we weren’t interested in linear or cable [TV].”

	David Ellison’s Skydance Media ended up buying Paramount — and now Paramount is trying to swing a $111 billion deal to merge with Warner Bros. Discovery. About industry consolidation, Ahuja said he’s “not too concerned about it.” 

	“Look, I think for us as a supplier to different companies, if for example hypothetically you went down to two or three companies, yeah, that’s not great. But I think to me, it’s more about the health than it is about the absolute number. Because I think we’ll have more than four [studios], for example. And I think it’s more about the health of the remaining companies that they are active buyers with us. Our biggest buyers are the biggest streamers, the ones that you’d expect, and I think they’re they’re in great shape. So it’s not something I lay awake at night thinking about.”
	

	During his talk, Ahuja also noted that Sony Pictures Entertainment recently combined all its YouTube groups together. YouTube is “a partner, not a competitor” for Sony Pictures Entertainment — again, because SPE does not have a general entertainment streaming business. 

	For example, SPE has launched a “Jeopardy!” YouTube edition that is runs a few times a year, hosted by Ken Jennings, featuring YouTube influencers competing with each other in the game show. “And by the way, the people that watch that extremely young, so it’s people in their teens and 20s,” Ahuja said. “And they know ‘Jeopardy!’, but they’ve hardly seen it. So this is an opportunity for them to see it.”

	“I think that YouTube, as a percentage of total viewing, will continue to grow,” Ahuja said.

	While it doesn’t have a Netflix competitor, Sony Pictures Entertainment operates the subscription streamer Crunchyroll, with Sony Music Entertainment Japan’s Aniplex, and the service recently surpassed 21 million paid subscribers. “Anime has become one of Sony Group’s most important growth areas,” Ahuja said. For Crunchyroll, “we think there’s a lot more growth ahead, and the Crunchyroll will continue to be a growth engine for us.”

title: Martin Herlihy Exits ‘SNL’ After Five Seasons

body:
Martin Herlihy is leaving “Saturday Night Live” after five seasons, a source confirms to Variety.

	The comedian served on the writing staff for Season 51 after spending four seasons on screen as a member of the sketch trio Please Don’t Destroy.

	NBC declined to comment.

	As part of a cast overhaul after Season 50, “SNL” split up Please Don’t Destroy, with John Higgins departing the NBC series and Ben Marshall getting upped to main cast. Herlihy remained on staff as a writer, appearing on screen periodically with sketches like “Blowing It” and “Green Flags” as well as a few of his “A Film by Martin Herlihy” pieces.
	

	With Please Don’t Destroy, Herlihy acted in dozens of sketches, often playing a fictionalized version of himself. He sparred with Dakota Johnson in the fan-favorite “Roast” sketch and was deemed a “sad virgin” by Taylor Swift.


	While Herlihy, Higgins and Marshall no longer share the screen on NBC, Please Don’t Destroy is still an active comedy trio that tours and pursues projects outside of “SNL” together. The three co-starred in the Peacock movie “Please Don’t Destroy: The Treasure of Foggy Mountain” in 2023, and Herlihy’s recent film credits have included “The Breadwinners,” “Roommates,” “The Running Man” and “Happy Gilmore 2,” which was co-written by his dad, longtime Adam Sandler collaborator Tim Herlihy.

	Herlihy is the second major departure ahead of “SNL’s” upcoming Season 52, following Chloe Fineman’s exit in July. Fineman, who is known for her impressions of Jennifer Coolidge and Drew Barrymore, among others, left Studio 8H after seven seasons.
	

	LateNighter broke the news of Herlihy’s exit.

title: Beloved Los Angeles Coyote Euthanized After Vets Discover She Was Shot In Face
description:
Beloved L.A. Coyote
                          Put Down After Being Shot in Face
body:
Beloved L.A. Coyote
                          Put Down After Being Shot in Face
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 9, 2026
                            8:20 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A beloved Los Angeles-area coyote named Wendy survived being shot in the face ... but the damage was so horrific that vets ultimately had to put her down.
      
    
            The 3-year-old coyote had become a familiar sight around Studio City, where locals noticed a huge growth on the side of her face and wildlife rescuers spent weeks trying to catch her.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Once they finally did, vets discovered the awful truth ... Wendy had been shot with a pellet gun, and two pellets were still lodged in her head.
      

            Even worse, the wound had caused a massive infection that destroyed part of her upper jaw.
      
    
            Rescuers hoped they could treat Wendy and release her back into the wild ... but vets determined the damage was too severe, and she'd never be able to eat normally or survive on her own again.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            So after she toughed it out with the injury for more than a year, Wendy was euthanized.
      
    
            A heartbreaking end for one seriously resilient coyote ... all because someone decided to use her for target practice.

            Spencer Pratt may have taken a fat L in the Los Angeles mayoral race, but he's considering the rumored cancellation of "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" as a win.
      
    
            The reality-star-turned-failed-politician went on Twitter to mock Jimmy Kimmel over the speculation ... aiming a stray at Gavin Newsom, too.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            Spencer wrote ... "Newsom AND Kimmel gone next year?? Be still, my laughing heart! Things are looking UP fam"
      

            As we previously reported, reports surfaced that ABC was not expected to renew Jimmy's contract once his current deal runs out in May 2027 ... and a source tells us there's talk among the staff that Jimmy has been working on pitching other shows and podcasts around town.
      
    
            However, the network is denying the rumor ... calling it speculation.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Spencer and Jimmy traded jabs throughout the 'Hills' alum's bid for mayor ... with the late-night host celebrating his loss by decorating a U-Haul in hopes Spence would be packing his bags.
      
    
            But if Jimmy really is hanging it up, this marks the end of a 24-year era that started all the way back in 2003 and Spencer Pratt's biggest L.A.-based victory to date.

title: Atlanta Freeway Crash Ends With Person's Legs Hanging Over Edge of Bridge
description:
Atlanta Freeway Crash
                          Couldn't Leg It From Crash Scene
body:
Atlanta Freeway Crash
                          Couldn't Leg It From Crash Scene
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 9, 2026
                            8:10 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            It seems The Flintstones have moved to Atlanta ... because someone's legs were spotted sticking out of the bottom of a car after a shocking crash!
      
    
            Insane footage obtained by Fox 5 Atlanta shows a car wedged between concrete pillars and dangling above traffic on a busy bypass in Atlanta ... with a passenger's feet hanging out of the car.
      
    
          Waiting for your permission to load TikTok Post.
      
    
            The car's on its side as it's perched precariously above the ground ... and bystanders warn the folks in the car to be careful not to come crashing down.
      

            The fellas who spoke to Fox 5 say it reminded them of "The Wizard of Oz"... when the Wicked Witch of the East's legs stick out from under Dorothy's house after it crushes her.
      
    
            Thankfully, this person won't have the same tragic ending as Nessarose's ... because cops say no major injuries were reported.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In fact, after first responders stabilized the car, the person was able to walk away from the crash site without any assistance. They were taken to a local hospital but suffered no critical injuries.
      
    
            We're not pulling your leg here ... all's well that ends well.
      
    
            The best part ... folks who first noticed the crash were leaving Atlanta's famous strip club, Magic City!!!

body:
Gun-Wielding National Guardsman
                          Tells Colleague He's Gonna Slap 'The Jackson 5 Out Of You'!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 9, 2026
                            5:54 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A National Guardsman got arrested and charged with 2 felonies after pulling a gun on a fellow Guard member and vowing to "slap the Jackson 5" out of her, according to an arrest affidavit.
      
    
            The affidavit, obtained by TMZ, stated that Zion Mitchell was apprehended by police last week and charged with assault with a dangerous weapon and possession of a firearm after a judge issued an arrest warrant for him.
      
    
            The alleged incident occurred on August 25, when Mitchell got into a heated argument with a female National Guard member while they were on break from patrol inside a van parked outside a Popeyes restaurant in D.C., according to cops.
      

            Police say the two argued over whether their hairstyles followed Army regulations, prompting Mitchell to tell the woman that he would “slap the Jackson 5 out of [her].” The woman allegedly replied, “Shut the f*** up. Try me."
      
    
            Suddenly, the woman heard a "holster click," cops say, and a third Guard member in the van allegedly stated, “Put that up. You almost shot me in the hand." It was only later the woman learned from her colleagues that Mitchell had allegedly drawn his pistol, which she believed was loaded.
      
    
            During his police interview, Mitchell initially told cops he and the victim were engaged in a "playful banter" when he pulled out a magazine from his pistol, according to the affidavit.
      
    
            But then Mitchell allegedly changed his story, saying he actually drew his sidearm and aimed it in the direction of the woman.

            The owner of a Florida doggy daycare has been arrested after employees found a hidden camera in the bathroom.
      
    
            Dog Dayz Inn owner Donald Hemphill was charged after the camera was found inside an electrical outlet on Saturday.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            During the Volusia Sheriff's Office Child Exploitation Unit's investigation, Hemphill allegedly copped to installing the camera about 4 or 5 months ago.
      

            The VSO says multiple videos were found that showed unknowing female victims in "stages of undress." Authorities say one subject was a child.
      
    
            Hemphill has been charged with 10 counts of digital voyeurism and 11 counts of video voyeurism of a child.
      
    
            According to the Volusia Sheriff's Office Hemphill is being held without bond.
